summary.text: Memorylessness is a property of some probability distributions: past failures or elapsed time do not affect future trials or further wait time.
Only two distributions have it: the geometric in the discrete case and the exponential in the continuous case.
It models the number of coin flips until landing heads and the time between two earthquakes.

facts.label: Discrete case
facts.value: The geometric distribution is the only memoryless one

facts.label: Continuous case
facts.value: The exponential distribution is the only memoryless one

facts.label: Coin example
facts.value: Number of flips until the first heads

facts.label: Converse
facts.value: A memoryless continuous distribution must be exponential

items.prompt: You flip a fair coin and get five tails in a row. In a memoryless model of flips until heads, what does that history do to the next flip?

options.label: It has no effect on the next flip
It makes heads more likely next
It makes heads less likely next
It makes the coin unfair

items.explain: Memorylessness means the number of previous failed trials has no effect on future trials.

items.prompt: Someone says a long quiet stretch without an earthquake makes one more likely soon. Under a memoryless model of time between earthquakes, what is true?

options.label: The elapsed time raises the chance of one
The elapsed time lowers the chance of one
The elapsed time has no effect on the future wait
The elapsed time makes the model invalid

items.explain: The elapsed time is independent of, and has no effect on, the further wait time.

items.prompt: You count the number of independent flips needed to land the first heads, and the count is memoryless. Which distribution is it?

options.label: Exponential
Normal
Uniform
Geometric

items.explain: The geometric distribution is the only discrete memoryless distribution.

items.prompt: A waiting time is measured on a continuous scale and is known to be memoryless. Which distribution must it follow?

options.label: The exponential distribution
The geometric distribution
The normal distribution
The uniform distribution

items.explain: If a continuous distribution is memoryless, it must be the exponential distribution.

items.prompt: Someone proposes a normal distribution as a memoryless model for waiting times. Why does that fail?

options.label: Normal curves cannot be graphed
Normal curves always have a mean of zero
Waiting times are always normal anyway
Only the geometric and exponential are memoryless

items.explain: Only the geometric and exponential distributions are memoryless.

items.prompt: Which statement best captures what memorylessness means?

options.label: The wait so far changes nothing about the wait still to come
The longer you wait, the sooner the event must arrive
Each wait must be exactly as long as the one before
The event can only occur once during the wait

items.explain: It describes situations where elapsed time or previous failures do not affect future trials or further wait time.
